label: 0017 · Starter, 50 km BEL cut, Tohoku-latitudes-only BEL sheet (35.5–41.5°N), UNR positions (exploratory MCMC)
description: starter_belcut50_jtonly_unr on Jack Loveless's 30 km BEL sheet bounded by the Japan Trench mesh's 30 km contour, 35.5N and 41.5N (87ee88c6), so there is also no BEL beneath Kanto, Tokai, northernmost Tohoku or Hokkaido. 938 of 976 triangles are kept after the forearc cut; 338 modes keep 99% of the prior variance. The fit after Tohoku is 27% worse than 0016's (median), almost entirely in Hokkaido north of 42.5N, where residuals rise from about 3 to 10 mm/yr: the stations move 7-16 mm/yr further west and 2-7 mm/yr further north than the model, a misfit that grows from 2012 to 2025. The interseismic windows, where the BEL is off in every experiment, show no consistent offset there (mean east residual -1.8 to +3.5 mm/yr), so unlike Kyushu's this is a post-Tohoku signal, which the BEL beneath Hokkaido absorbs in 0016. Dropping the BEL beneath Kanto and Tokai changes little. The remaining sheet slips 1.5-4 times faster, most of all far from the stations. Trench afterslip reaches Mw 8.35 at 2 yr, with half as much first-year afterslip in the main rupture (0.43 m instead of 0.92). w015-w022 have max R-hat 1.10-1.31 from a few slowly mixing BEL eigenmode coefficients: new Noto mesh, UNR IGS20 positions, same 596 GEONET sites and windows
